source.quote: Servers that support tools MUST declare the `tools` capability:
When the list of available tools changes, servers that declared the `listChanged` capability SHOULD send a notification:

requirements.exclusion: The trigger condition — the tool list actually changing — is server-internal state a recorded trace cannot evidence, so absence of the notification is never proof of violation.

source.quote: `inputSchema`: JSON Schema defining expected parameters; MUST be a valid JSON Schema object (not `null`)
For trust & safety and security, clients MUST consider tool annotations to be untrusted unless they come from trusted servers.

requirements.exclusion: How a client weighs annotations is internal trust policy with no wire footprint.

source.quote: Tool names SHOULD be between 1 and 128 characters in length (inclusive).
The following SHOULD be the only allowed characters: uppercase and lowercase ASCII letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), underscore (_), hyphen (-), and dot (.)
Tool names SHOULD NOT contain spaces, commas, or other special characters.
Tool names SHOULD be unique within a server.
Servers that use embedded resources SHOULD implement the `resources` capability:
For backwards compatibility, a tool that returns structured content SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a TextContent block.
If an output schema is provided: Servers MUST provide structured results that conform to this schema.
Servers MUST: Validate all tool inputs; Implement proper access controls; Rate limit tool invocations; Sanitize tool outputs

requirements.exclusion: Input validation, access control, rate limiting, and output sanitization are server-internal enforcement without a deterministic wire signature. Of the four duties, mcp-everything-server implements and tests input validation (tests/roundtrip.rs: tool_call_with_missing_required_argument_is_a_protocol_error and neighbors); access control beyond the transport-layer Host/Origin gate, rate limiting, and output sanitization are not in its scope — it serves fixed synthetic fixtures to a loopback-only harness.

source.quote: Tool names SHOULD be considered case-sensitive.

requirements.exclusion: Name-comparison semantics are consumer-internal; tools.name-unique (TOOL-008) applies case-sensitive comparison in accordance with this clause.

source.quote: Clients SHOULD validate structured results against this schema.

requirements.exclusion: Client-side validation has no wire footprint; the server-side half of the contract is TOOL-011's check.

source.quote: For trust & safety and security, there SHOULD always be a human in the loop with the ability to deny tool invocations.

requirements.exclusion: A host application's approval UX is outside the protocol session; a trace shows invocations that happened, not the approvals that gated them.

source.quote: Applications SHOULD: Provide UI that makes clear which tools are being exposed to the AI model; Insert clear visual indicators when tools are invoked; Present confirmation prompts to the user for operations, to ensure a human is in the loop

requirements.exclusion: Binds the application's user interface — what it shows, when it asks, whether a person is there. None of it is a message, and MCP deliberately does not mandate an interaction model.

source.quote: Clients SHOULD provide tool execution errors to language models to enable self-correction.

requirements.exclusion: Binds what the client hands to a language model, which is downstream of the session entirely.

source.quote: Clients SHOULD: Prompt for user confirmation on sensitive operations; Show tool inputs to the user before calling the server, to avoid malicious or accidental data exfiltration; Validate tool results before passing to LLM; Implement timeouts for tool calls; Log tool usage for audit purposes

requirements.exclusion: Five client-side practices — confirmation prompts, showing inputs, validating results, timeouts, audit logs. Each happens inside the client or in its UI; none is a message.
